executive_summary.text: Market size (TAM): USD 1.8 billion (AI crop disease detection market, 2025).
Demand: Most small farmers say they lose crops because diseases are spotted late.
Priority segment: Smallholder farmers. They feel the crop losses most directly.
4 competitors found: 1 direct, 2 indirect and 1 emerging.
Possible gap (medium confidence, a hypothesis): Few competitors show treatment advice tailored to the diagnosed disease.
Main limitation: A free photo diagnosis app is already available.
Main risk (high severity, market): Farmers stay with the free app.
First release, the top 3 of 4 features: Photo-based diagnosis, Treatment advice and Local language support.
Go-to-market, start here: Short demo videos on a messaging app.

verify_next.text: Find a reliable market size for this idea's own market: no source confirmed the SAM or SOM.
Look for stronger market sources: the market evidence was rated limited.
Find out more about Fasal: the sources gave little detail.
Test the low-confidence gap: No competitor in the results mentions offline diagnosis.
Check the high-severity risk "Farmers stay with the free app", which has low confidence. Early warning sign: Pilot users raise farmers stay with the free app in interviews.
Check the high-severity risk "Wrong diagnosis on poor photos", which has low confidence. Early warning sign: Pilot users raise wrong diagnosis on poor photos in interviews.
Confirm your team size and timeline: the MVP plan assumes a team of 2 people and 3 months to the first release.
Run the first experiment for Short demo videos on a messaging app: Try short demo videos on a messaging app with a few farmers for two weeks.

swot.summary: The idea meets a clear farmer problem. Free alternatives make adoption the main question.

strengths.text: The app diagnoses crop disease from a single phone photo.
Treatment advice comes with every diagnosis.
Local language support lowers the barrier for rural users.

weaknesses.text: The concept relies on farmers owning a camera phone.
Diagnosis quality depends on training images not yet collected.
A small assumed team limits field testing.

opportunities.text: Late diagnosis is a widely reported farmer problem.
Advice in local languages is still an open niche.
Cooperatives could distribute the app to their members.

threats.text: An established free diagnosis app already serves farmers.
Public helplines give free advice by phone.
Drone scouting services may reach cooperatives first.

gtm.summary: Start with smallholder farmers through short videos and cooperatives. The plan rests on a pilot that shows farmers act on the advice.

positioning.problem: spot crop diseases too late to save the harvest
positioning.key_benefit: names the disease and a treatment from one photo
positioning.alternative: free diagnosis apps and phone helplines
positioning.differentiator: it pairs each diagnosis with treatment advice in the farmer's language
positioning.statement: For smallholder farmers on rain-fed plots who spot crop diseases too late to save the harvest, CropScan: AI crop disease detection is a photo diagnosis app that names the disease and a treatment from one photo. Unlike free diagnosis apps and phone helplines, it pairs each diagnosis with treatment advice in the farmer's language.
